mutant.description: The arm whose pass could most easily be a constant is (e): 'the protected record is unmoved' would read the same whether the record moved or not if it compared the wrong property. So the arm compares SHA256 OF THE SERVED BYTES rather than VersionIds -- because restoring a pin is a copy-object, which mints a NEW VersionId carrying the pinned CONTENT. A check on 'IsLatest == the pinned id' would FAIL on a correctly-restored record; one on 'IsLatest is unchanged' would PASS on any copy whatever it copied.
mutant.expected: Each protected key's served bytes must sha256-match its recorded pin, and the run's OWN version must differ from the pin -- otherwise the comparison cannot tell a restored record from an unrestored one.
mutant.observed: All three protected keys match their pins by sha256 while the run's own version differs (dbe02e28c705f3eb against the pin's 9d0ff4d6135a9ccb), so the comparator distinguishes the two states.
